raw_case_text: A 17-year-old male recipient of matched-sibling donor transplant for myelodysplastic syndrome, on immunosuppressive agent, presented with fever and body ache on day +317. Donor chimerism at day +180 was >90%. At presentation, CBC showed Hb = 16.5 g/dL, hematocrit (HCT) = 48%, platelet = 90 x 109/L. Physical examination revealed harsh vesicular breathing. Dengue NS1 antigen was detected. Blood cultures were negative. He was managed conservatively for 1 week as inpatient with intravenous hydration, analgesics, and antipyretics. Platelet count dropped to 24 x 109/L followed by recovery without need for transfusion.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 17-year-old male hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipient presented on day +317 post-transplant with fever and body ache.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who underwent matched-sibling donor transplantation for myelodysplastic syndrome and remained on immunosuppressive therapy, presented on post-transplant day +317 with acute fever and generalized body aches.
subjective.past_medical_history: Myelodysplastic syndrome status post matched-sibling donor stem cell transplant (day +317; donor chimerism >90% at day +180).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever and body ache. Home medication: immunosuppressive agent.

objective.routine_investigations: At presentation: hemoglobin 16.5 g/dL, hematocrit 48%, platelet count 90 x 10^9/L (subsequently dropping to a nadir of 24 x 10^9/L). Blood cultures were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Dengue fever in a post-allogeneic stem cell transplant recipient, confirmed by positive dengue NS1 antigen and negative blood cultures. Managed conservatively as an inpatient for 1 week with intravenous hydration, analgesics, and antipyretics, achieving full platelet count recovery from a nadir of 24 x 10^9/L without platelet transfusion.
